state.case_summary:
An obese man in his mid-30s with no prior systemic or ocular disorders presented to a local emergency department after waking with vision loss in his right eye. The night prior, he had been drinking alcohol heavily and took 2 buprenorphine hydrochloride/naloxone hydrochloride pills. He denied any trauma. He also experienced pain, numbness, and erythematous induration of his right eyelids and forearm that increased throughout the day.

Visual acuity: No light perception in right eye (OD) and 20/20 in left eye (OS). Right eye showed tense eyelid edema, chemosis, corneal haze, and restricted motility in all fields of gaze. Right pupil was mid-dilated with a relative afferent pupillary defect. Intraocular pressure was 37 mm Hg OD and 21 mm Hg OS. Ophthalmoscopic examination revealed tortuous vessels, serous retinal detachment sparing the inferior periphery, and macular whitening. Left eye examination was normal.

- Laboratory Tests:
Creatinine level: 2.2 mg/dL
Creatine kinase level: 29,320 U/L

- Imaging Studies:
1. Noncontrast computed tomography of head and orbits: Showed periorbital soft-tissue swelling

2. Optical Coherence Tomography:
Image Title: OCT of the Right Eye
Image Description: Demonstrates severe disorganization of the retinal architecture, subretinal fluid, and sub-retinal pigment epithelial fluid

3. Fluorescein Angiography:
Image Title: Fluorescein Angiography of the Right Eye
Image Description: Shows delayed choroidal filling, delayed retinal arterial filling, patchy temporal hyperfluorescence, diffuse leakage and poor vascular perfusion in various phases

root.label: Acute Unilateral Vision Loss with Ocular and Orbital Compromise
supporting_facts: Pain, numbness, and erythematous induration of the right eyelids and forearm
Tense eyelid edema, chemosis, corneal haze, and restricted motility in all fields of gaze
Intraocular pressure was 37 mm Hg OD and 21 mm Hg OS
Serous retinal detachment sparing the inferior periphery, and macular whitening
excluded_candidates: Ischemic optic neuropathy: less likely due to the presence of orbital and ocular compromise
Central retinal artery occlusion: less likely due to the presence of tortuous vessels and serous retinal detachment
Globe rupture: less likely due to the absence of trauma history
alarm_features: Signs of orbital and ocular compromise
salient_findings: No light perception in right eye
Severe disorganization of the retinal architecture, subretinal fluid, and sub-retinal pigment epithelial
Delayed choroidal filling, delayed retinal arterial filling, patchy temporal hyperfluorescence, diffuse leakage
